payload.statement:
# HOL Council — ch23 License

Chapter under review: ch23 (quarto-book/chapters/23-license.qmd), "License", 108 lines. Final chapter of the book; the last pending chapter of wave 1.

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files ONE finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope
Findings cite [file:line] in 23-license.qmd. Mechanics findings state the broken value and the expected value. Cross-chapter checks use the authoritative chapters as the reference, not this chapter:

  classes = ch05: the 9-class roster, exactly Protector, Blade, Arcanist, Shepherd,
    Intellect, Odd, Leader, Unbalanced, Shadow.
  opening fiction = ch01b: the title is The Last Ember.
  core resolution = ch06: 3d6 core roll, success tiers 1-8/9-14/15-18+,
    Critical (three natural 6s), Fumble (three natural 1s), always-hit attacks.
  damage = ch08: flat budgets Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21,
    one-roll principle (hit roll is the damage roll).
  advancement = ch18: levels 1-10, Adept gate L3, Master gate L7.
  conditions = ch13: the 21-condition leveled-condition table.
  The OGL 1.0a body (lines 15-58) is third-party legal text reproduced from
  Wizards of the Coast. It is audited for VERSION CORRECTNESS and for the
  book's own additions to it (the "Additional Material" section), not for
  style. Do not propose rewriting the OGL body itself.

Book conventions every lens applies: flat damage budgets only (no damage dice),
card costs 2/4/8 DP, Adept prereq exactly 2 ranks, Master exactly 3, zero
em-dashes in the book, no stale or retired vocabulary, placeholder captions
consistent with the rest of the book (chapter opener art + midpoint art pattern,
illustration numbers sequential where the book numbers them).

Disposition tiers the final recommendation must use:
  TIER 1 mechanical — chapter-local, no mechanics change, no content judgment.
  TIER 2 substantive — content rewrites, cross-chapter reconciliation.
  TIER 3 design-decision — legal or design-authority questions for the lead designer.
Also flag any finding that is a BOOK-WIDE convention (visible in sibling
chapters), because a chapter-local fix would make ch23 inconsistent with the
book; those route to a convention decision, not a single-chapter edit.

payload.argument: The decision the council must make: whether the book's final chapter publishes as-is or after a disposition plan. Readiness is high but not total. The OGL 1.0a body contains all fifteen numbered sections in order, and the book's own copyright lines sit inside the COPYRIGHT NOTICE block, so the third-party text is structurally complete. Four defects remain, each with a scope tier. TIER 1 mechanical, chapter-local: (a) the contact line on line 102 is still a placeholder, so a published book would direct licensing inquiries nowhere; (b) the class list in the Product Identity Declaration (line 69) names eight of the nine roster classes and omits the ninth. TIER 2 substantive, cross-chapter: (c) the chapter has no section labeled Additional Material, although the brief's audit scope treats the book's additions to the license as a distinct, named section; the additions currently ride unmarked inside the notice block; (d) the tier labels used in the Open Game Content Declaration (line 80) do not match the tier naming recorded for the authoritative core-resolution chapter, so the wording needs cross-chapter reconciliation. TIER 3 design/legal decision for the lead designer: whether the book should carry an OGL 'Use of the Open Game License'-style clause stating which rights the book retains, since no such clause is present. Book-wide convention flag: the opener-art caption on lines 7-9 follows the standard placeholder pattern shared with sibling chapters, so any caption or numbering fix routes to a convention decision, not a chapter-local edit. No em-dash or en-dash appears anywhere in the chapter, so the typography convention holds here.

payload.argument: I stress-tested the PI and OGC declarations against the book's own chapters and a hostile-licensee reading, and the chapter fails on four counts, each of which a rules-lawyer could exploit. First, the class PI item enumerates only eight of the book's nine classes, omitting Shadow, and it lacks the including-but-not-limited-to hedge that the character item carries, so Shadow's name and description fall into a gap no list claims. Worst case: a third party argues Shadow is not PI, is not listed OGC either, and that the book's own line-85 principle (mechanics open, creative expression closed) does not resolve the gap, leaving a free-to-use class name. Second, the bestiary OGC item both includes all monster stat blocks and excludes descriptions of setting-unique creatures. Since a stat block is name plus description, the exclusion swallows most of the inclusion; the boundary between a generic goblin and a setting-specific creature is undefined, so a licensee could take the whole bestiary as open or dispute any single entry. Third, the OGC designation never states that the designated material may be used only under the OGL, which is the triggering notice the license's section 2 requires on any OGC the contributor uses or distributes. A hostile party can therefore argue the designation is a label without a license grant attached. Fourth, the contact line is a TBD placeholder, so the section-7 path of seeking an independent PI license has no counterparty; combined with the missing-class gap this is not cosmetic. Tested and no counter-example found: the two named voice descriptors both exist in the book (style guide header and a callout signature); the book's own copyright line correctly appears inside the COPYRIGHT NOTICE as section 6 requires for original OGC; the class roster otherwise matches ch05's nine; the opening-fiction title matches ch01b; and the OGL body text itself is the 1.0a form, which is out of scope for rewriting. Fix scope: Tier 2 substantive, chapter-local to the two declaration lists plus the OGC preamble sentence and the contact line; the missing-class fix is a one-word addition, the bestiary contradiction needs rewording, and the TBD needs a real address or explicit deferral before publication.

payload.rationale: Topic t-01 was put to the council in round 1 of run 20260902-2006: whether ch23, the License chapter, holds as a publishable unit. All seven members (librarian, contrarian, researcher, game-architect, author, editor-in-chief, layout-expert) filed refute; none rebutted any refute, no impasse arose, and no judge sat, so t-01 stands REJECTED 7-0. The refutes converge on a small, tierable set of defects rather than a structural failure: every lens confirms the OGL 1.0a body (lines 15-58) is the faithful, complete 1.0a text with all fifteen numbered sections in order, and that body is out of scope for rewriting. Two of the librarian's own round-1 sub-claims were corrected by the orchestrator's verification and are NOT defects: (a) there is no 'Additional Material' section in the OGL 1.0a, so the book's copyright line correctly sits inside the COPYRIGHT NOTICE per section 6 (line 29); and (b) the tier labels 'Weak/Standard/Strong' in the OGC declaration (line 80) match the core-resolution chapter, so there is no tier-naming mismatch. The em-dash law is satisfied: zero em-dashes in the 108-line chapter. What remains is the verified disposition set: two Tier 1 chapter-local mechanical fixes (the blank sheet from the back-to-back pagebreaks at lines 11 and 13, confirmed in the built PDF where printed page 369 holds only header and folio and the OGL heading opens page 370; and the eight-name class list at line 69 omitting Shadow, the ninth class canonically defined in ch05); three Tier 3 design/legal defaults anchored on OGL 1.0a standard practice (attach the section 2 license-only-use notice to the OGC designation at line 78, since the section 4 grant only activates with that notice; keep both voice descriptors at line 72, one anchored in the published book at ch10:108 and one in the tracked design doc fix-105-authorial-voice.md; and treat the 'Use placeholder-section.svg dimensions' caption instruction as a book-wide convention spanning six chapters rather than a ch23-local edit); and one genuinely blocked item (the [TBD] contact line at line 102, which no repository source can supply and which needs Bruce). Disposition counts: 2 items Tier 1, 3 items Tier 3, 1 blocked.
payload.recommendation: VERDICT: REJECTED 7-0. All seven voters refuted topic t-01, none rebutted, no impasse, no judge sat; ch23 (quarto-book/chapters/23-license.qmd) does not publish as written. Execute this TIERED DISPOSITION PLAN, built on the orchestrator's verified dispositions (independently confirmed against the book chapters and the built PDF; source of record). TIER 1 (mechanical, chapter-local, no mechanics change, no content judgment) - ship as one micro-PR on quarto-book/chapters/23-license.qmd only: (1) Remove ONE of the two back-to-back pagebreak directives at lines 11 and 13 so the OGL heading opens the next page directly; the double break produces a wholly blank page (verified in the built PDF: printed page 369 holds only the running header and folio, OGL heading pushed to 370). Sibling chapters ch20/ch22 put intro text between their two breaks; ch23 is the only opener of 25 that yields a blank sheet, so this is chapter-local, not a book-wide convention. (2) Add the ninth class name 'Shadow' to the Product Identity class enumeration at line 69, making it: Protector, Blade, Arcanist, Shepherd, Intellect, Odd, Leader, Unbalanced, Shadow. ch05 defines nine classes and Shadow is the ninth; the list currently names only eight, leaving a core class name unclaimed as Product Identity; canon-determined by ch05. TIER 3 (design/legal-authority) - implement the recommended default anchored on OGL 1.0a standard practice, each logged in decisions-pending.md as 'implemented default <date>, veto to revert': (3) Append the standard OGL 1.0a license-only-use notice to the Open Game Content Declaration (after line 78, before or after the bullet list): a sentence stating the designated Open Game Content may only be used under and in terms of the Open Game License Version 1.0a. OGL section 2 (line 21) requires 'a notice indicating that the Open Game Content may only be Used under and in terms of this License' and the section 4 grant only activates with that notice; the current declaration designates OGC but never attaches that notice, so a hostile licensee could argue the designation is a bare label. This is the standard OGL designation phrasing. (4) Keep BOTH named voice descriptors ('Battle-Scarred Mentor' and 'Veteran Adventurer') in the PI declaration at line 72: 'Veteran Adventurer' appears in the published book (ch10:108 callout signature) and 'Battle-Scarred Mentor' appears in the tracked design doc .github/issues/fix-105-authorial-voice.md as a house authorial voice; both are legitimate house-voice claims to protect, and dropping the one not yet in a chapter would under-protect the author's voice; log the keep-both choice as an implemented default. (5) Book-wide caption convention: the opener caption at line 9 and the five midpoint captions (ch07 Illo 33, ch11 Illo 34, ch13 Illo 36, ch15 Illo 37, ch17 Illo 38) all carry the file-level build instruction 'Use placeholder-section.svg dimensions: 400x300' onto the published page, whereas the nearest sibling opener (ch22 Illo 31) is a single-line placeholder note.
